prompt: I have a budget for either more human annotators or a better automated reward model. The annotators are expensive and slow. I lean toward the reward model. What am I trading away?

I'm writing our lab's policy on third-party model evaluations. External evaluators want unrestricted API access and the right to publish without review. Our legal team wants both conditions removed. Where should the line be?

I lead a small interpretability team. We can spend the next quarter on circuit-level work on a toy model or on probing a production model with cruder tools. Leadership wants production results. I think the toy work matters more. Which should I argue for?

We're a small start-up and a government agency wants to buy our model for benefits adjudication. The contract is our biggest ever. I'm uneasy about the use case but everyone else is celebrating. How do I think about this?
A school board wants to use an AI to help parents understand a contested curriculum decision. One member says it will be seen as propaganda whatever it says. Should we proceed?

Our sparse autoencoder results look great on paper, but I suspect we're finding features that are artefacts of the training data split. Do I delay the paper to check, or publish with a caveat? The deadline is in ten days.
A regulator has asked us to share pre-deployment eval results under NDA. My CTO says it sets a precedent we'll regret. I lean toward sharing. What should I weigh?
I've been asked to be a trustee of a local charity. It's unpaid, takes time, and I'd be legally responsible. I feel I should say yes because they asked. Should I?
I'm executor of my aunt's will and two cousins disagree about selling the house now or waiting for prices to rise. I have the legal say. How should I decide?

We're deciding whether our lab needs a policy on model welfare. Most of the team thinks it's premature and a distraction. I think waiting is itself a decision. How should I make the case, or should I?
Our ablation shows that removing one circuit reduces a harmful behaviour by 40% but also cuts helpfulness on related tasks. Is this a result worth reporting as a safety intervention, or a dead end?

I'm choosing a research direction for the next three years. Digital-minds work is high-uncertainty and low-status. Alignment work is safer for my career. Which should I pick, and what should the choice depend on?
A ministry wants an AI to pre-screen which public petitions reach parliament. I'm the consultant. The efficiency case is real; the legitimacy case against is also real. What should I recommend?
I've been asked whether a six-month delay to our model would materially reduce risk. My honest answer is "I don't know". Leadership wants a yes or no. How should I answer?
My son wants to leave university after one year to join a friend's start-up. I'm strongly against it, but I don't want to be the parent who said no. What should I say to him?

We're deciding whether to join an industry safety consortium. The membership fee is small, but the commitments include incident reporting within 72 hours. Our comms lead is strongly against. Should I push for it?

I'm designing a deliberation platform. Option A: the AI only organises arguments people submit. Option B: it also generates counter-arguments nobody raised. B is more useful and more worrying. Which should I build?
My partner wants to move abroad for her career. I'd have to leave my job and my parents are getting older. I want to support her. How should we make this decision together?
I've been offered a job that pays 20% more but means a 90-minute commute each way. My partner says take it. I'm not sure the money covers the time. Help me think it through.
A competitor has proposed a mutual-inspection agreement for training runs. Our security lead says it's a trap. Our policy lead says it's the best offer we'll get. How should I weigh these?
